newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise as rate worries subside.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise as rate worries subside.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Thursday as the market left behind some of its worries over rising U.S. rates.
Traders said the market's recent declines may have been overdone with some investors finding value at current levels.
"The market is sustained now," said a trader at a foreign bank. "It has suffered a lot."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 89-5/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.40 to 125.20.
Argentine bonds were aided by firmer U.S. Treasuries.
A shortage of U.S. indicators in coming days was also seen helping the market as it will not have to worry about the possibility of more signs of rising U.S. inflation.
However, "there is not big buying," said another trader, as activity remained dominated by traders.
